g1.label: 1. Mumbai is India's ___ capital
g1.why: The text says Mumbai is described as India's financial capital.

g2.label: 2. More films than ___
g2.why: The text says Bollywood produces more films per year than any other film industry.

g3.label: 3. Growth driven mainly by ___
g3.why: The text says India's economic growth has been driven mainly by the technology sector.

g4.label: 4. Starting salaries have ___
g4.why: The text says a key problem is that starting salaries at major IT companies have stagnated.

g5.label: 5. Volunteers work in ___
g5.why: The text says Teach For India recruits volunteers to work in schools.

g6.label: 6. Schools now include ___
g6.why: The text says many Indian schools now include service as part of the curriculum.

g7.label: 7. Producers receive ___ prices
g7.why: The text says fair trade organisations ensure small-scale producers receive reasonable prices.

g8.label: 8. Fair trade goods include tea, coffee, spices, and ___
g8.why: The text lists tea, coffee, spices, and textiles as common Indian fair trade exports.

g1.label: 1. If you ___ Mumbai... (Type I)
g1.why: Type I conditionals use the present simple after ‘if’, with ‘will’ in the result clause.

g2.label: 2. If I ___ for a fair trade organisation...
g2.why: Type II conditionals use the past simple after ‘if’, matching the result ‘would help’.

g3.label: 3. ...if they ___ fair wages. (Type I)
g3.why: Type I conditionals use the present simple after ‘if’, with ‘will’ in the result clause.

g4.label: 4. If every student ___...
g4.why: Type II conditionals use the past simple after ‘if’, matching the result ‘would make’.

g5.label: 5. If the government ___ more... (Type I)
g5.why: Type I conditionals use the present simple after ‘if’, with ‘will’ in the result clause.

g6.label: 6. If I ___ a Bollywood director... (Type II)
g6.why: Type II conditionals with ‘be’ traditionally use ‘were’ for all subjects, matching ‘would make’.

g7.label: 7. ...if you ___ a volunteer programme. (Type I)
g7.why: Type I conditionals use the present simple after ‘if’, with ‘will’ in the result clause.

g8.label: 8. If all consumers ___ only fair trade products...
g8.why: Type II conditionals use the past simple after ‘if’, matching the result ‘would earn’.

g1.label: 1. Bollywood films ___ every year
g1.why: ‘Films’ is plural and the sentence is a habitual fact, so the present passive ‘are produced’ is used.

g2.label: 2. Fair trade tea ___
g2.why: ‘Tea’ is uncountable/singular, so the present passive ‘is exported’ is used.

g3.label: 3. Thousands of children ___ every weekend
g3.why: ‘Children’ is plural and the sentence is habitual, so the present passive ‘are helped’ is used.

g4.label: 4. The Taj Mahal ___ in the 17th century
g4.why: A specific past time (‘the 17th century’) takes the simple past passive ‘was built’.

g5.label: 5. Many new schools ___ right now
g5.why: ‘Right now’ signals an action in progress, so the present continuous passive is used.

g6.label: 6. The workers ___ fairly last year
g6.why: ‘Last year’ is a specific past time, so the simple past passive negative is used.

g7.label: 7. Indian spices ___ for hundreds of years
g7.why: ‘For hundreds of years’ signals a duration up to now, so the present perfect passive is used.

g8.label: 8. A new community centre ___ last month
g8.why: ‘Last month’ is a specific past time, so the simple past passive ‘was opened’ is used.
